Subject: Lumen Health — renewal & scale handoff / QBR scheduling

Hi Priyanka / Marcus —

Hope you’re both well. We’re kicking off the renewal & scale conversation for Lumen’s Feb refresh window and I wanted to get a short-run timeline + QBR on the calendar so we can align stakeholders and locking in capacity targets. High-level items we want to cover:

- Confirm committed capacity / anticipated 90-day uplift (we’ve seen initial signal that you may need +25–30%).
- Discuss term options (you mentioned flexibility; common asks: 12 vs 18 months).
- Present mutual action plan (MAP) and pricing options for committed + burst.
- QBR: operational runbook, onboarding timeline for any capacity changes.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm primary stakeholders we should invite to the kickoff/QBR (technical, procurement, finance).
2) Pick a 60–90 min QBR slot during the week of Feb 13–17 — I can hold Feb 14 or Feb 16 as options; I’ll send a calendar poll once you confirm.
3) We’ll follow up with two pricing options and an updated MAP for your review before the QBR.

I’m copying Marissa (pricing lead), Monica (CS), and Rishi (solutions) so they can prepare the estimate and runbook. I’ve attached an initial MAP draft and a one-page checklist to accelerate legal/PO prep.

Attachments: Lumen_MAP_v1.pdf (draft MAP), QBR_calendar_poll.ics (placeholder)

Thanks — happy to set up a short call this week if that helps.

Best,
Diego Fernández

Subject: Re: Lumen Health — renewal & scale handoff / QBR scheduling (internal)

Diego / team — looping here with pricing ops notes so we can move quickly once Priyanka confirms. Key assumptions from Priyanka: +30% throughput and request for 18-month option. Quick thoughts:

- Offer A (12m): modest uplift pricing, standard onboarding, no burst credits.
- Offer B (18m commit): 8–12% committed discount off list for steady-state, plus a small burst credit pool (prepaid tokens) and an onboarding service credit. We should bucket burst credits into monthly allotments so ops can track.
- If they want guaranteed throughput SLA at the higher tier, we’ll need dedicated capacity blocks — price these as a separate line item.

Action items:
1) Rishi — build the run-rate for +30% for both offers and include a dedicated capacity line.
2) Ben — prepare a short note on delivery risk and onboarding timeline (if they take dedicated capacity we should allow a 4–6 week ramp).
3) Legal — prep a lightweight amendment template we can prefill.

Let’s target sending both options + estimate to the customer by EOD Feb 4.

Marissa
Head of Deals | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Diego Fernández <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-02-04T10:55:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Lumen Health — pricing scenarios & estimate (internal)

Folks — attached is the estimate workbook (Lumen_estimate_v1.xlsx). Summary highlights:

- Baseline run-rate (current): $142k / month.
- Scenario +30% throughput: incremental $42.6k / month (assuming same model mix); 12m total ARR ~ $2.09M.
- 18m commit discount options: 10% off committed token spend + 3 months of burst credits (prepaid) yields effective blended unit cost reduction of ~12%.
- Dedicated capacity block (optional): additional $32k / month but reduces p95 latency and removes cross-tenant noisy neighbor risk. 4–6 week delivery.

Recommendation to send to customer: present both (12m vs 18m) and call out dedicated block as an optional add-on — give them clear cost/latency tradeoffs.

I’ll prep a one-page run-rate for the pre-read.

Rishi
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
